He played [[college basketball]] for [[Eastern Oklahoma State College|Eastern Oklahoma State]] and [[Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball|Illinois State]]. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=6}}, he usually plays the [[small forward]] position. == College career == Akoon-Purcell transferred from [[Eastern Oklahoma State College]], where he was a National Junior College Athletic Association (NJCAA) Division I All-America Honorable Mention selection in 2014, to [[Illinois State University]] ahead of the 2014–15 season.{{Cite web|url=https://goredbirds.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1261|title=Illinois State Athletics|website=goredbirds.com|language=en|access-date=2018-08-16}} During his junior season at Illinois State, Akoon-Purcell was named to the [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC) All-Newcomer Team,{{Cite web|url=https://goredbirds.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4139|title=Illinois State Athletics|website=goredbirds.com|language=en|access-date=2018-08-16}} and he was also named the MVC Newcomer of the Year.{{Cite news|url=https://www.pantagraph.com/sports/college/basketball/men/isu-s-akoon-purcell-earns-mvc-newcomer-of-year-award/article_7de6fa00-a8d9-5473-9083-94a298016e89.html|title=ISU's Akoon-Purcell earns MVC Newcomer of Year award|last=Benson|first=Jim|work=pantagraph.com|access-date=2018-08-16|language=en}} In 2014–15, he was also a finalist for the Riley Wallace Award, presented annually to the top transfer in [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] Division I basketball, as awarded by [[Collegeinsider.com|CollegeInsider.com]].{{Cite web|url=https://goredbirds.com/news/2015/3/31/MBB_0331155927.aspx|title=Akoon-Purcell Named Finalist for Riley Wallace Award – Illinois State University|website=Illinois State University|date=31 March 2015 |language=en|access-date=2018-08-16}} Ahead of his senior season, Akoon-Purcell was a 2015–16 MVC Preseason Team selection.{{Cite news|url=http://www.wjbc.com/2015/10/27/isu-picked-4th-in-mvc-akoon-purcell-named-to-valley-preseason-team/|title=ISU picked 4th in MVC, Akoon-Purcell named to Valley preseason team|date=2015-10-27|work=WJBC AM 1230|access-date=2018-08-16|language=en-US}} During his senior season at Illinois State, Akoon-Purcell led the team in scoring and ranked eighth in the MVC with 14.1 points per game on his way to earning All-MVC Second Team and NABC Division I District 16 Second Team accolades. Akoon-Purcell went undrafted in 2016.{{Cite web |last=Gauruder |first=Dana |date=7 August 2018 |title=Nuggets Sign DeVaughn Akoon-Purcell To Two-Way Deal |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2018/08/nuggets-to-sign-akoon-purcell-to-two-way-deal.html |access-date=2018-08-16 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US}} ==Professional career== ===Bakken Bears (2016–2018)=== In August 2016, Akoon-Purcell signed a one-year contract with Danish side [[Bakken Bears]] of the [[Basketligaen]] and [[FIBA Europe Cup]].{{Cite news|url=http://goredbirds.com/news/2016/8/17/mens-basketball-akoon-purcell-signs-pro-contract-with-danish-team.aspx|title=Akoon-Purcell Signs Pro Contract with Danish Team|publisher=Goredbirds.com|date=17 August 2016|access-date=31 March 2018}} He led the Bears to a Basketligaen championship in his first season, while being named the league's MVP and Finals MVP.{{Cite web|url=http://www.goredbirds.com/news/2017/5/9/mens-basketball-akoon-purcell-leads-bakken-to-danish-title-named-finals-mvp.aspx|title=Akoon-Purcell Leads Bakken To Danish Title, Named Finals MVP|date=5 September 2017|publisher=Goredbirds.com|access-date=31 March 2018}} In his second season with the Bears, he reached the semi-finals of the FIBA Europe Cup and won the Basketligaen championship. Akoon-Purcell was given the title of Fan Vote FIBA Europe Cup MVP, as he received 4,939 fan votes. He also was named the Guard of the Year of the competition.{{cite web | title=Winners of FIBA Europe Cup Fan Vote announced | website=FIBA.basketball | date=19 April 2018 | url=http://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/17-18/news/winners-of-fiba-europe-cup-fan-vote-announced | access-date=10 August 2018}} ===Denver Nuggets (2018)=== Akoon-Purcell joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] [[NBA Summer League]] roster ahead of the 2018 Las Vegas Summer League, averaging 12.0 points, 2.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 2.0 steals in 19.3 minutes per game. On August 7, 2018, the [[Denver Nuggets]] signed Akoon-Purcell on a two-way contract.{{cite web | title=Nuggets Sign Rookie DeVaughn Akoon-Purcell to Two-Way Contract – Denver Nuggets | website=Denver Nuggets | date=7 August 2018 | url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-akoon-purcell-080718 | access-date=10 August 2018}} Akoon-Purcell played in only 7 games with the Nuggets throughout the entirety of his two-way contract. On December 16, 2018, after the expiration of his two-way contract, he was waived by the Nuggets.{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Brandon Goodwin, Waive DeVaughn Akoon-Purcell|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-goodwin-waive-akoon-purcell-121618-3|website=NBA.com|date=December 16, 2018|accessdate=December 17, 2018}} ===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2018–2019)=== On December 19, 2018, Akoon-Purcell signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] for the rest of the season.{{cite web|title=רכש נוסף לאדומים: דבון אקון-פרסל|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=19660|website=basket.co.il|date=December 19, 2018|accessdate=December 19, 2018|language=he}} However, on February 19, 2019, Akoon-Purcell parted ways with Hapoel after appearing in eight games.{{cite news|title=American forward DeVaughn Akoon-Purcell has left Hapoel Tel Aviv|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/american-forward-devaughn-akoon-purcell-has-left-hapoel-tel-aviv/|newspaper=Sportando|date=February 19, 2019|accessdate=February 19, (2019)=== On March 9, 2019, Akoon-Purcell signed with [[ESSM Le Portel]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]].{{cite news|title=DeVaughn Akoon-Purcell signs with ESSM Le Portel|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/devaughn-akoon-purcell-signs-with-essm-le-portel/|newspaper=Sportando|date=March 9, 2019|accessdate=March 9, 2019 |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola }} In 12 games played for Le Portel, he averaged 9.1 points and 2.5 rebounds per game. ===Oklahoma City Blue (2019–2020)=== On September 30, 2019, Akoon-Purcell signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://okcthunderwire.usatoday.com/2019/09/30/thunder-add-four-players-prior-training-camp/|title=Thunder add four players prior to training camp|access-date=October 5, 2019|work=OKCThunderWire|date=September 30, 2019}} He was cut from the team in the preseason and was signed by their G League affiliate, the [[Oklahoma City Blue]]. On January 21, 2020, Akoon-Purcell posted 33 points and 7 rebounds in a 125–116 win over the [[Austin Spurs]].{{cite news |title=Oklahoma City Blue top Austin Spurs |url=https://www.statesman.com/sports/20200121/oklahoma-city-blue-top-austin-spurs |accessdate=June 13, 2020 |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=January 21, 2020}} The following game, he scored 38 points while adding eight rebounds, two assists and one steal in a 144–140 loss to the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite news |title=DeVaughn Akoon-Purcell: Seeing expanded role |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/devaughn-akoon-purcell-seeing-expanded-role/ |accessdate=June 13, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 24, 2020}} ===Tofaş (2020–2021)=== On September 2, 2020, Akoon-Purcell signed a one-month deal with the [[Bakken Bears]].{{cite news |title=DeVaughn Akoon-Purcell returns to Bakken Bears for BCL qualifiers |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/devaughn-akoon-purcell-returns-to-bakken-bears-for-bcl-qualifiers/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=September 2, 2020 |date=September 2, 2020 |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola }} However, on September 29, he signed with [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] of the Turkish league.{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Tofas sign Devaughn Akoon-Purcell |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/646392/Tofas-sign-Devaughn-Akoon-Purcell |website=Eurobasket |accessdate=September 29, 2020 |date=September 29, 2020}} Akoon-Purcell played for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[2021 NBA summer league]], scoring 13 points in 27 minutes on 6–9 shooting and grabbing 8 rebounds and 2 steals at his debut in a 85–83 loss against the [[Boston Celtics]] and former Hapoel Tel-Aviv teammate [[Yam Madar]].{{Cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Atlanta Hawks Aug 8, 2021 Box Scores {{!}} .255 || .718 || 5.2 || 4.3 || 1.6 || .0 || 18.6 |} ==Personal life== Akoon-Purcell was born to parents Paul Akoon Jr. and Tamar deGovia-Purcell.{{cite web |last1=Benson |first1=Jim |title=ISU's Akoon-Purcell carrying those not with him on Senior Night |url=https://pantagraph.com/sports/college/basketball/men/isus-akoon-purcell-carrying-those-not-with-him-on-senior-night/article_e2733366-159d-5f4c-bfeb-770043056278.html |website=The Pantagraph |access-date=December 1, 2023 |date=February 24, 2016}} He moved in with his grandparents when he was aged 11.{{cite web |title=Bears profile lost the people who turned him into a basketball player |url=https://www.bakkenbears.com/2016/11/14/bears-profile-lost-the-people-who-turned-him-into-a-basketball-player/ |website=Bakken Bears |access-date=December 1, 2023 |date=November 14, 2016}} His grandmother died in April 2013; Akoon-Purcell wore a #44 jersey to honor her as she died on the fourth month of the year and he was her fourth grandchild. Akoon-Purcell also began to use his full name after her death as he was previously known as DeVaughn Purcell. Akoon-Purcell has tattoos on each wrist dedicated to his grandmother and his former coach [[Torrey Ward]] who was killed in a plane crash in April 2015. Ward recruited Akoon-Purcell out of Eastern Oklahoma State in 2014.
